messages:
jordan: thanks everyone for joining the pricing section. a few Qs came up — dropping the live Q&A thread here.

alison: quick one — how does burst behavior work for starter vs paid tiers? if we hit a burst, are we throttled or charged from credits?

sam_finance: to add: what's the ordering between using prepay credits, free trial credits, and postpay billing?

raj_eng: technical TL;DR: two controls — short-term rate limiter (tokens/sec) and long-term quota buckets (monthly credits). starter tier has tighter rate limits; bursts are allowed up to a window but will be rate-limited if you exceed per-second caps.

raj_eng: example we return on rate limit:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 12
{
  "error":"rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message":"per-account QPS exceeded"
}
```

raj_eng: if you run out of quota (credits) you'll get a quota error with guidance to add credits or request lift — we surface what was consumed.

jordan: adding policy notes: hosted API prefers fairness — free tiers -> strict caps; paid tiers -> larger soft caps + credit drawdown. we don't auto-upgrade anyone. for enterprise/dedicated we offer contractual SLOs and configurable bursts.

sam_finance: credits order: 1) promo/free trial credits 2) prepaid balance 3) postpay billed usage (only for approved customers). so bursts first consume any trial/prepay.

alison: what's the fastest way for a partner to get a temporary quota lift for an evaluation?

kim_prod: process: file a request with solutions-eng or sales, we can issue 3–14 day trial lifts. for longer term we recommend Dedicated or a committed usage plan. roadmap: planning self-serve quota requests for dashboards in Q3.

alison: perfect — thanks.

ops-bot: Slides and notes from today's all-hands are uploaded: https://docs.redwood.com/inference/all-hands/2025-pricing. See 'burst policy' section.

sam_finance: i'll update the billing FAQ with the credits precedence and an example invoice flow.

raj_eng: followup engineering note for anyone integrating: prefer exponential backoff + jitter on 429s, don't spin on 402/quota-exceeded — surface to user or fallback model.

kim_prod: i'll create a short doc snippet and add to the quickstart prompts about recommended retry/backoff patterns.

alison: thanks team :thumbsup:

jordan: thanks, we'll post an updated FAQ + runbook by end of next week. if anyone needs an exception DM me or @sales.

sam_finance: noted — pinged sales to coordinate partner lifts.
